original_definition.name: token checking overlaps classification, while small requests and hard locks need no count call

previous_coverage_row.name: token checking overlaps classification, while small requests and hard locks need no count call

evidence.scope: All121 Router instances/263 routes and29 pure calls. Complete native policy decisions, actual classifier/cache/count execution and full captured synthetic transport requests. Four literal JavaScript API/clock boundaries remain partial.

remaining_assertions: Original source synchronously enters countTokens before fetchImpl. Native replay verifies both endpoint counts, full payloads and no-count small/locked paths; existing semaphore regression proves overlap/reuse. Neither proves the same JavaScript callback-start ordering across asynchronous native transport scheduling.

per_assertion.native_predicate: For original-shaped 160K system/Haiku request, actual count transport enters before evaluator, and both count and evaluator remain pending concurrently; count response40000 and Haiku decision are checked.
The selected model remains the configured Haiku after a 40000-token count; source Jev decision, context_check and unchanged document are asserted.

per_assertion.source_expression: assert.fail('Must not add a counting request')
per_assertion.native_predicate: Frozen captured tiny and large enabled-thinking/hard-lock branches replay through actual classifier/count transport and issue no count request.

native_API_review.preserved: An admitted speculative count starts before classifier evaluation for the original suspicious request, then both unresolved transport responses overlap. Tiny and enabled-thinking locked requests do not count.
native_API_review.migration: JavaScript immediately invokes a caller-owned countTokens callback before fetchImpl; Rust spawns a native owned TokenCounter task and awaits an acknowledgement after its real future has been polled. No JavaScript callback or promise identity is claimed.
native_API_review.capacity_limit: If bounded advisory task capacity is exhausted, the native router may skip speculation and classify before a required later count. This saturation case is not in original definition #51 and remains a reviewed resource-policy difference; no universal count-before-evaluator claim is made.
native_API_review.performance_limit: First count poll performs synchronous serialization/cache work before evaluator admission; latency and unchanged performance gates require separate measurement.

scope: Only original router#51 is covered under the explicit native async API migration. Earlier router mappings remain historical; advisory-capacity saturation, numerical latency, complete platform or release gates are not promoted.
